body:
TASK-1293 WAS STRANDED A SECOND TIME, BY A DIFFERENT MECHANISM, TWENTY MINUTES AFTER I FIXED THE FIRST ONE.

  spec carried       batch:followups-0918i
  drain is running   queue work --auto-complete --batch night-0920

So after I requeued it, it sat correctly queued, correctly statused, and invisible to the only thing that could work it. Retagged to night-0920.

TWO INDEPENDENT STRANDINGS ON ONE SPEC IN ONE NIGHT, and neither was visible from the surface that would normally reveal it. The first: Done status with a held PR and no queue entry — the PR page shows a hold, not whether anyone owns the fix. The second: queued but filtered out — the queue shows an entry, not whether anything will read it.

I SWEPT FOR OTHERS and found none: every in-progress spec carrying a batch tag is on night-0920. So this was the only one, which is worth saying because "I found one" and "there is one" are different claims and I have been careful about that distinction all night.

THIS IS EXACTLY WHAT TASK-1297 REPORTS, and that merged tonight. Its fix makes a drain announce the approved specs its `--batch` filter excludes, with reasons, at start-up. Once a drain runs with that code this becomes a line in the output instead of something I find by comparing a spec's tags against a lock file by hand. It was filed after a stale filter hid sixteen approved specs for hours — this is the seventeenth, found the old way, roughly six hours after we merged the fix that would have caught it.

That is a good argument for restarting the drain onto the current binary at some point, though I am not asking for it mid-wave: the running drain launched before TASK-1297, BUG-1305, BUG-1290 and the rest landed, so none of tonight's orchestration fixes are in the process actually orchestrating. Everything I have merged improves the NEXT wave, not this one.

Nothing else this tick. No mail, no rework on #2003, #2006 or #2009, drain at phase 3 on BUG-1310.
